nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori proposed trapping neutral atoms in an optical lattice tuned to a 'magic' wavelength, so that the clock transition is unperturbed by the trapping light. This combines the large atom numbers of neutral ensembles with the confinement of a single trapped ion. Katori and Ye turned the concept into working strontium clocks. Ye's group pushed systematic uncertainty and stability down to the 10^-18 to 10^-19 level and introduced degenerate Fermi-gas and spin-squeezed operation. These clocks are now about a thousand times more precise than the caesium standard that defines the SI second. They resolve gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences, provide relativistic geodesy, and constrain variations of fundamental constants and couplings to dark matter. They are driving the redefinition of the second. This is a new measurement paradigm: the most precise instruments ever built, opening tests of fundamental physics through time itself.
